subject: Intro / Demo request — inference for search ranking (follow-up questions)
messages:
From: Jordan Smith <jordan@pqtech.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-12T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Demo request — inference for search ranking

Hi Connor,

We signed up for a trial yesterday and would love to see Redwood in action for our search-ranking inference use case. Quick background: we run a product search that serves ~120k sessions/day and peak concurrent requests around 70-120 QPS during sales events. We care about sub-80ms latency on median and cost per 1k tokens is important for our finance team.

Can we schedule a 30–45 minute demo and a quick pre-demo Q&A to confirm throughput expectations? We're aiming to evaluate vendors over the next two weeks with a target pilot start in October.

Attached a CSV with anonymized traffic slices.

Cheers,
Jordan
Director, ML Platforms
PQ Tech
[attachment: traffic_snapshot_Q3.csv (csv)]

From: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Smith <jordan@pqtech.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-12T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo request — inference for search ranking

Hi Jordan — thanks for the context and the traffic CSV, that helps a lot. Ben (copied) will join the demo for the pilot & pricing discussion. A few quick questions so we can tailor the demo and prepare a throughput estimate: 

1) Typical sequence lengths for your ranking model (tokens)? Any heavy prompts / system messages we should expect?
2) Do you need embeddings + reranking as part of the flow, or just token-generation ranking scores?
3) Is SSO / SCIM required for the pilot, or can we run with standard token access initially? If SSO, can you share the SAML metadata?
4) When you say 70-120 QPS at peak, is that sustained for more than a minute (e.g., a 10–30 minute sale spike) or short spikes (seconds)?

Proposed demo windows (PST):
- Tue Sep 14, 10:00–10:45
- Tue Sep 14, 14:00–14:45
- Wed Sep 15, 11:00–11:45

If those don't work, tell me the best 3 windows your team has and we'll accommodate. We'll cover architecture, batching/latency behavior, cost levers (quantization/batching/caching), and a short Q&A.

Also attached a one-pager on typical pilot deliverables.

Best,
Connor
SDR, Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood_pilot_onepager.pdf (pdf)]

From: Jordan Smith <jordan@pqtech.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-13T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo request — inference for search ranking

Connor — thanks, this is great. Quick answers inline: 

1) Sequence lengths: ranking model input average ~220 tokens, worst-case ~1.1k (we truncate above 1.2k). System messages are minimal.
2) We use an embedding store + re-ranker stage. Ideally we'd see both paths.
3) SSO not mandatory for the pilot; token-based is fine to start. Will need SSO for production. We'll share SAML metadata later.
4) Spikes: typically sustained for 10–20 minutes during campaigns.

We can do Tue Sep 14 at 14:00 PST — that works for our infra and ML leads. I've included pqtech-platform@pqtech.com on this thread for calendar invites.

Jordan

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Smith <jordan@pqtech.com>, connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-14T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo request — inference for search ranking

Jordan — thanks for locking the 14:00 PST slot; we've sent a calendar invite to pqtech-platform@pqtech.com. For the demo we'll prepare:

- A short perf run using a synthetic traffic slice derived from your CSV to show expected median/p95 latency at 50/100 QPS.
- Two flow paths: embeddings + reranker, and direct re-ranking generation.
- Expected cost ballpark for a 30-day pilot at your daily sessions (approx).
- Notes on scaling strategies during 10–20 minute spikes (burst pools + autoscale).

Quick ask before the call: if you can, please share a single example request/response (redacted) that represents a typical ranking request — just the input tokens and the expected output format. That lets us validate sequence-length assumptions and reproduce it in the perf run.

See you Tue at 14:00 PST — invite includes a dial-in and a shared doc for live notes.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[attachment: sso_requirements.pdf (pdf)]
